Sparked by a dispute over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg throne, this 1740–1748 conflict began when Prussia seized the wealthy province of Silesia — what was this conflict called?
War of the Austrian Succession: 1740–1748 war between European powers.

Despite a huge edge in tanks and aircraft, the Soviet Union took heavy losses and was expelled from the League of Nations after its November 1939 invasion of Finland — what was this three-and-a-half-month conflict called?
Winter War: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland.
A career Army general who became a national hero in the Mexican-American War, this 12th U.S. president died of a stomach illness just 16 months into office — who is he?
Zachary Taylor: President of the United States from 1849 to 1850.

Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.

Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.

What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year did Niels Bohr die?
Niels Bohr: Although the Bohr model has been supplanted by other models, its underlying principles remain valid.
In what year was Fluorine discovered?

Who is credited with discovering Technetium?

Who is credited with discovering Cell theory?

Sharing the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces, who became the first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel?
Abdus Salam (29 January 1926 - 21 November 1996) was a Pakistani theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate.
This exaggerated immune reaction causes the body to mistake a harmless substance for a threat, triggering symptoms from a runny nose to a full anaphylactic reaction — what is it?
Allergy is an exaggerated immune response where the body mistakenly identifies an ordinarily harmless allergen as a threat.
These eusocial insects evolved from vespoid wasps back in the Cretaceous, and you can spot one by its elbowed antennae and pinched, node-like waist. Which creature is it?
Ant are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae and, along with the related wasps and bees, belong to the order Hymenoptera.
With atomic number 85 and symbol At, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, forming only as a decay product of heavier elements — name it?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
Native to South American tropical forests, this thorny ornamental vine, bush, or tree produces large colorful bracts surrounding three small waxy flowers — what is this plant genus?
Bougainvillea (US also BOH-) is a genus of thorny ornamental vines, bushes, and trees belonging to the family Nyctaginaceae.
Originating from the now-discredited caloric theory of heat, this unit of energy is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius — name the unit?
Calorie is a unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.
This class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed body segments called proglottids into the environment to infect new hosts — what is this class called (scientific name)?
Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This American investor and podcaster coined the phrase 'intellectual dark web' and proposed a physics framework called 'Geometric Unity' — who is he?
Eric Weinstein (born October 26, 1965) is an American investor and podcast host.

Native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, this fig species carries deep religious significance across four faiths that originated there, including reverence from Hindu and Jain ascetics — what species is it?
Ficus religiosa is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
One of only two wild camelid species native to South America, this llama relative lives at lower elevations than its cousin, the vicuña — what is it called?
Guanaco (gwah-; Lama guanicoe) is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.
Never approved by any drug regulator, this THC-like compound made by hydrogenating cannabis isomers has been sold in head-shop vaporizers since the early 2020s — what is it?
Hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) is a phytocannabinoid that has been reported as a minor component of Cannabis oleoresin.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.

Spread by the bite of sandflies and caused by a genus of protozoal parasites, this tropical disease can present as skin ulcers, disfiguring mucosal damage, or a more dangerous internal form. Name the disease?
Leishmaniasis is a wide array of clinical manifestations caused by protozoal parasites of the Trypanosomatida genus Leishmania.
This evergreen tree, native to the cooler hills of south-central China, is grown commercially for its orange fruit and is sometimes called the Japanese medlar. What is it?
Loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
Following fieldwork with the Omaha people and in Papua New Guinea and Bali, this anthropologist explored gender roles in her 1935 book Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies — who is she?
Margaret Mead (December 16, 1901 - November 15, 1978) was an American cultural anthropologist, author and speaker, who appeared frequently in the mass media during the mid-twentieth century.
Despite little formal education, this self-made English scientist established the concept of the electromagnetic field and uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction — who is he?
Michael Faraday (22 September 1791 - 25 August 1867) was an English chemist and physicist who contributed vastly to the study of electrochemistry and electromagnetism.
This group of more than 30 rare neuromuscular disorders causes skeletal tissue to progressively weaken and break down, differing in which body parts are hit first and how fast — what's it called?
Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a genetically and clinically heterogeneous group of rare neuromuscular diseases that cause progressive weakness and breakdown of skeletal muscles over time.
This raised region of tissue on the breast, surrounded by the darker-colored areola, is where milk exits the body through the lactiferous ducts during breastfeeding — name this body part?
Nipple is a raised region of tissue on the surface of the breast from which, in lactating females, milk from the mammary gland leaves the body through the lactiferous ducts to nurse an infant.
Usually caused by bacteria and sometimes requiring amputation in severe cases, this infectious inflammation of bone can be acute or chronic — which condition?
Osteomyelitis (OM) is the infectious inflammation of bone. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Recognized by a long beak and an enormous throat pouch used to drain water from scooped-up prey before swallowing, these large water birds come in eight living species worldwide — which birds?
Pelican (genus Pelecanus) are a genus of large water birds that make up the family Pelecanidae.
What small, tailless, round-bodied mountain mammal — a close relative of the rabbit with short rounded ears — includes a large-eared Himalayan species that lives above 6,000 meters?
Pika is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.
A zoonotic virus that triggers violent movements, a dread of water, and almost certain death once symptoms set in — usually one to three months after exposure. What is this disease?
Rabies is a zoonotic viral disease that causes acute and severe encephalitis in humans and other mammals.
This British economist won the 1991 Nobel Memorial Prize and warned that the field was "suicidal" to become a hard science of choice while ignoring society, history, and culture — who was he?
Ronald Coase (29 December 1910 - 2 September 2013) was a British economist and author.
Which leathery-skinned marine echinoderm, of which about 1,786 species are known worldwide, plays a vital ecological role on the sea floor by breaking down detritus as a scavenger?
Sea cucumber are echinoderms from the class Holothuroidea.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

This chalcogen element, chemically similar to selenium and sulfur, is far more abundant in the universe than on Earth because its hydride escaped into space during our planet's formation — which element?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Dolphins, porpoises, beaked whales and sperm whales all belong to this cetacean group that diverged from baleen whales around 34 million years ago — what's the collective name?

Toothed whale (also called odontocetes, systematic name Odontoceti) are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth, such as beaked whales and the sperm whales.
As head of the WWII Office of Scientific Research and Development, this MIT engineer steered nearly all American military R&D, including radar and the early Manhattan Project — who was he?
Vannevar Bush (van-; March 11, 1890 - June 28, 1974) was an American engineer, inventor and science administrator, who during World War II headed the U.S.

This bird family, which also includes piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers, is absent from Australia and Madagascar, though one desert-dwelling member has adapted to drill into cacti — what family of birds is it?
Woodpecker are part of the bird family Picidae, which also includes the piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers.

This organic compound functions as a neurotransmitter in the brain and body of many animal types, including humans. It is the chemical that motor neurons release at the neuromuscular junction to enable muscle movement. What is it?
Acetylcholine: Organic chemical and neurotransmitter. Its name is derived from its chemical structure: it is an ester of acetic acid and choline.
Born in 1929 and died in 2001, this man was a respected Saudi Islamic scholar — who is he?

Native to South Africa's Western Cape, this flowering bulb genus lends its common name to popular winter houseplants that actually belong to a different genus, Hippeastrum — which bulb, also called the naked lady or Jersey lily?
Amaryllis: Genus of plants. Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
This category of illness occurs when the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue, with more than 80 recognized forms identified so far — what's the category?
Autoimmune disease: Disorders of adaptive immune system. Autoimmune diseases are a separate class from autoinflammatory diseases.
Spurred by the 1980 failure of Operation Eagle Claw, this American tiltrotor blends a helicopter's vertical takeoff with a turboprop's long-range cruise — what aircraft is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey: Military transport tiltrotor.
This insect order unites cockroaches with termites, after genetic evidence showed termites are actually evolved, eusocial cockroaches. What's the order called?
Blattodea: Order of insects that includes cockroaches and termites.
Making up just 2.6 percent of the brain's weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and houses all ten pairs of cranial nerve origins — what is it?
Brainstem: Posterior part of the brain, adjoining and structurally continuous.
This silvery-gold alkali metal has a melting point just above room temperature, making it one of only five elemental metals that go liquid in warm conditions — what is it?
Caesium: Chemical element with atomic number 55 (Cs)
This Cornell astronomer worked on the Mariner, Viking, and Voyager missions and won a Pulitzer for 'The Dragons of Eden' — who is this famed science communicator?
Carl Sagan: American scientist and science communicator (1934–1996)
Known commonly as tapeworms, this class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed segments called proglottids — what is this class called?
Cestoda: Class of flatworms. Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Produced mainly by the adrenal cortex and surging in response to stress and low blood sugar, this steroid hormone is sold as medicine under the name hydrocortisone — what is it?
Built from microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules, this network gives a cell its shape and lets it contract and migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton: Network of filamentous proteins that forms the internal framework of cells.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
Element 105 sparked a long Cold War naming dispute, claimed first by a Soviet institute in 1968 and then by Berkeley in 1970 before being settled in 1993 — which synthetic element?
Dubnium: Chemical element with atomic number 105 (Db)
The first woman admitted to MIT, this environmental chemist was the first to apply chemistry to nutrition and founded the home economics movement — who was she?
Ellen Swallow Richards: American engineer and chemist (1843–1911)
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen drives the development of secondary sexual characteristics and helps maintain reproductive tissues from puberty through pregnancy — what is it?
Known for its smooth silvery-grey bark and toxin-laced but edible nuts, this deciduous tree native to Europe includes the striking copper-leaved cultivar among its ornamentals — which species?
Fagus sylvatica: Species of deciduous tree. It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
The only venomous lizard native to the United States, this sluggish reptile from the Southwest rarely poses a real threat despite its fearsome reputation — what is it?
Gila monster: Largest species of lizard in the United States.

Native from Mexico down to southern Brazil, this large arboreal lizard can grow past six feet long, is a popular but demanding pet, and has become invasive in many warm regions worldwide — which species?
Green iguana: Species of reptile. Usually, this animal is simply called the iguana.

Named after a bird of prey, this British-developed attack aircraft was the only truly successful vertical-takeoff design of its era, able to fly from car parks and forest clearings instead of vulnerable airbases — which aircraft?
Harrier jump jet: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace.
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This huge insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, and its females often carry an egg-laying tube that doubles as a stinger — what order is it?
Hymenoptera: Order of insects. Over 150,000 living species of Hymenoptera have been described, in addition to over 2,000 extinct ones.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.
Sometimes called the founder of pneumatic chemistry, this 17th-century Brussels physician coined the word 'gas' and ran a famous five-year willow-tree experiment. Who was he?
Jan Baptist van Helmont: Chemist and physician (1580–1644)
Equal to the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre, this SI unit of energy is named for a 19th-century English physicist — which unit?
Joule: SI unit of energy. The joule ( JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.
Also called dragon's eye, this tropical fruit tree from the soapberry family produces fruit similar to lychee but with a milder aroma, and is native to Southeast Asia and southern China — what is it?
Longan: Species of tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes and caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, which disease's symptoms typically begin 10 to 15 days after infection?

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Sold in extended-release form under the brand name OxyContin, this highly addictive semi-synthetic opioid treats moderate to severe pain and brings relief within about fifteen minutes. What is it?
Oxycodone: Opioid medication. It is usually taken orally, and is available in immediate-release and controlled-release formulations.
Prized wood from this fruit tree's genus, Pyrus, is a favorite material for making high-quality woodwind instruments, and China grows about three-quarters of the world's crop — which fruit?
Pear: Edible fruits from the genus Pyrus.

First described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the "cellar spider" and "vibrating spider" — and shares a famous leggy nickname with harvestmen and crane flies. What family is it?
Pholcidae: Family of spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.

Though crustaceans within this food category are more closely related to insects and spiders than to true fish, what group — including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms — ranks among the most common food allergens?
Shellfish: Culinary and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates.
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.
Also called oxolane, this colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether is a versatile solvent and polymer precursor — and an isomer of butanone. Abbreviated with three letters, what is it?
Discovered in Cornwall in 1791 and named after the Titans of Greek myth, this corrosion-resistant transition metal shrugs off seawater, aqua regia, and chlorine alike — what is it?
Titanium: Chemical element with atomic number 22 (Ti)

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
Described from Mongolian fossils in 1924 and smaller than relatives like Deinonychus, which feathered, sickle-clawed dinosaur genus roamed Late Cretaceous Asia?
Velociraptor: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924.
First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop — which grain?
Wheat: Genus of grass cultivated for grain. Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.
